newsitem.title: USA: US cattlemen hail decision on poultry water weight.
newsitem.headline: US cattlemen hail decision on poultry water weight.

text.p: Livestock producers Tuesday hailed a recent U.S. District Court ruling on poultry water weight saying it should help their case to have one inspection system for meat and poultry.

"Our goal is to have one meat inspection system for the meat and poultry industries," said Max Deets, president of the National Cattlemen's Beef Association, which issued a statement together with the National Pork Producers Council and the American Sheep Industry Association.
"One inspection system would help red meat producers more fairly compete with poultry," Deets said.
Currently, U.S. Agriculture Department regulations permit up to eight-percent water retention in poultry carcasses during chilling. No water retention is permitted in beef, pork or lamb carcasses.

U.S. District Court Judge Ronald Lonstaff in Des Moines, Iowa, ruled last week that the added-water regulations were "arbitrary and capricious" because USDA failed to adequately explain why meat and poultry should be treated differently.
